newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt hits peak, other Eurobourses down.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt hits peak, other Eurobourses down.

text.p: German stocks extended its record-breaking rally on Wednesday, but other European bourses slipped back, dogged by worries over interest rates. On currency markets, the dollar strengthened as traders took an optimistic view of the outcome of a policy-making meeting of the U.S. central bank and inflation indicators out later on Wednesday.
In Frankfurt, floor and screen trading both hit intra-day records, boosted by the strengthening dollar, which was seen as helping exports.

Computerised deals measured by the IBIS index registered a gain of 0.4 percent by midday as the dollar climbed decisively over the psychologically-important 1.50-mark level. The previous best of 2765.61 was set only on Tuesday in a late rally.
Floor trading was in a similar buoyant mood and the DAX index advanced rapidly to a trading high of 2775.12 points, eclipsing the record set last Friday.

German investors, already encouraged by the dollar's strength after supportive comments by German central bank officials, were further cheered when utility giant Veba reported a surprise 25 percent hike in nine-month net profits.
The news drove Veba shares up to a record 86.90 marks, spreading the mood of optimism.
But some analysts saw the momentum slackening. "The rally is feeding the rally, but today with somewhat less foaming at the mouth," said one dealer.
Tuesday's late IBIS rally came after comments by Bundesbank council member Edgar Meister that a dollar level below 1.50 marks was "not appropriate" boosted the U.S. currency.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks edged lower despite another record close on Wall Street, the fifth in succession. Trading was depressed by worries over interest rates.
Investors were focusing attention on the rate-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting that begins at 1400 GMT.

Most analysts expected the Fed would hold rates steady amid signs that the see-saw U.S. economy was settling down and this would be greeted with relief by global equity markets. New York's current bull run is rooted in this view.
A steeper-than-anticipated decline in British unemployment and unexpectedly strong unit wage costs revived concerns about inflationary pressures, further depressing markets.
"It does seem the labour market is pretty buoyant...The data underlines the overall recovery is becoming quite punchy," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell economist Ciaran Barr.
"Interest rates are going to go up early next year, the pressure is on for a 25 point rise before the election. It does make the case for a rate rise that much clearer."
Clues about inflationary pressures in the United States may also emerge from U.S. October producer prices due on Wednesday, with October consumer prices and retail sales comping out on Thursday.
In Paris, stocks slipped 0.5 percent at the opening following a year high struck on Tuesday. A large state sale of shares in Elf adding to consolidation pressures.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened against the mark and the yen, buoyed up by traders' optimism over the FOMC meeting.

"You almost have this Goldilocks scenario in the U.S. with solid sustainable growth and no inflation. Certainly in the near term I don't see that threatened," said Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon.
Analysts said the U.S. currency was also supported by comments on Tuesday from Bundesbank officials, including Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, supporting a firmer dollar.

"German industrial production figures have been weaker than expected. In light of that, the Buba is not going to want a strong Deutsche mark...I wouldn't rule out further cuts in repo rates further out," said Weatherby.
CURRENCIES AT 1220 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5063 marks and 111.42 yen, compared with 1.5015 marks and 111.38 yen in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1220 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 8.2 points lower at 3,926.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 39.43 points at 2,773.73.
PARIS - The CAC 40 index was down 8.97 points at 2220.16
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1220 GMT
Gold was fixed at $382.50, up from $381.75 at the London close on Tuesday. Silver was at $4.91, up four cents.
